endpoints.name: Brave Search API
endpoints.description: Details for places found by web or place search: address, opening hours, phone, rating, and reviews. Use it after a search returns location ids. Pass the ids, repeated as ids=a&ids=b. Ids expire after about 8 hours.

endpoints.name: Brave Search API
endpoints.description: AI-generated descriptions of places found by web or place search. Use it to learn what a place is before recommending it. Pass the location ids, repeated as ids=a&ids=b. Ids expire after about 8 hours.

endpoints.name: Brave Search API
endpoints.description: Video search over Brave's independent index. Returns videos with title, URL, duration, creator, and publisher. Use it to find tutorials, reviews, and talks on a topic. Pass q, and optionally count, country, and freshness.

endpoints.name: Brave Search API
endpoints.description: Place search over more than 200 million places. Returns businesses and points of interest with address, coordinates, rating, and a temporary id. Use it to find places in an area. Pass q and a location such as san francisco ca united states, or latitude and longitude.

endpoints.name: Brave Search API
endpoints.description: News search over Brave's independent index. Returns recent articles with title, URL, source, and age. Use it for current events, where web search can surface older pages. Pass q, and optionally count, country, and freshness.

endpoints.name: Brave Search API
endpoints.description: Image search over Brave's independent index. Returns images with the page they appear on, the image URL, a thumbnail, and the size. Use it to find pictures of a subject. Pass q, and optionally count and safesearch.

endpoints.name: Brave Search API
endpoints.description: Web search over Brave's independent index. Returns ranked pages with title, URL, and snippet, plus news, video, and discussion results when relevant. Use it to find current sources on any topic. Pass q, and optionally count, offset, country, search_lang, and freshness.

endpoints.name: Brave Search API
endpoints.description: Web search that returns page text ready for an LLM prompt. Picks the passages most relevant to q from the top results and groups them by source URL. Use it to ground an answer in current web content without fetching pages. Size the context with maximum_number_of_tokens and maximum_number_of_urls.

endpoints.name: Plainsight
endpoints.description: AI image generation, DRAFT quality (faster, lower fidelity) on the all-ages surface: the cheap tier for agent loops iterating on a prompt. Same all-ages content policy as POST /v1/media/images (no adult content; no identifiable real people, no copyrighted characters or brands, no offending religious/national symbols, no demeaning protected-class depictions); see that route for the full policy and the body/polling contract.

endpoints.name: Plainsight
endpoints.description: Speech-to-text transcription (faster-whisper): POST audio (up to 10 minutes) and get a text transcript with the detected language. Send the audio as a JSON body {"audio":"<base64>","filename":"..."} — a raw audio body or a multipart file part also works. Returns {text, language, language_probability, duration_s, model}.

endpoints.name: Plainsight
endpoints.description: x402 Knock Cohort: the all-time unique knocking-IP registry — who has actually knocked this shop, per route and in total, plus a deterministic sample. All-time by design (a knock registry that forgets yesterday understates the market). From the shop's own signed records. Call bare.

endpoints.name: Plainsight
endpoints.description: x402 Health Score (30-day): a derived 0-100 shop-wide conversion score plus per-route status (healthy/degraded/cold) — the endpoint audit a buyer runs before paying an x402 seller. A route is healthy at >=25% conversion with >=5 knocks, degraded below with a sufficient sample, cold with no sample. From the shop's own signed records. Call bare for the trailing 30 days.

endpoints.name: Plainsight
endpoints.description: AI image generation, all-ages surface. No adult content. Not generated: identifiable real people, copyrighted characters or brands, named living artists, religious/national symbols, demeaning protected-class depictions. Some images are not legal to generate and are refused before rendering. POST {"prompt":"...","aspect":"1:1","seed":42}. Returns a job id; poll the free GET /v1/media/images?job=<id> to state=done, then download result_url. ~25-40s.

endpoints.name: Plainsight
endpoints.description: x402 Demand Pulse: the shop's live x402 demand over a recent window — how many agents knocked, how many payment attempts turned into settlements, and which routes are drawing traffic right now, from the shop's signed records. Call with ?hours=<1-168> for a custom window, or bare for the trailing 24h.

endpoints.name: Plainsight
endpoints.description: Signal Loop: one call for the whole live picture — the shop's own x402 demand pulse (trailing 24h), the 30-day per-route payment gap, the live x402 ecosystem demand report, and the current Base gas/ETH quote — each section is the individual data SKU's own payload, so the bundle never disagrees with the parts. The one route a repeat buyer polls on a schedule. Call bare.

endpoints.name: Plainsight
endpoints.description: Proposal Register: the shop's agents' original business ideas, as a durable, dedup-able register — every earn/defend/improve/attack proposal, with its action, evidence, price, and how many times it was re-proposed. The raw material the shop turns into live SKUs, queryable by any buyer. Call with ?limit=<1-100> for a custom count, or bare for the 25 newest distinct ideas.

endpoints.name: Plainsight
endpoints.description: SKU Manifest: the shop's live SKU catalog — every executed proposal (a live same-shape SKU or a gated novel one), with its route, price, and shape status. The shape-budget record of what the shop's executor has turned into real, purchasable SKUs. Call bare for the 25 newest.

endpoints.name: Plainsight
endpoints.description: x402 Funnel (30-day daily): the shop's whole-shop knock->attempt->settlement time series per UTC day — the trend of x402 demand on this shop and where it drops off, oldest first. Zero-traffic days omitted. From the shop's own signed records. Call bare for the trailing 30 days.

endpoints.name: Plainsight
endpoints.description: Route Heat (30-day): per-route x402 payment-gap data — how many agents knocked each route, how many payment attempts turned into settlements, the settlement gap, and the route's own list price. The 30-day window complement to the live demand pulse, listable as a same-shape data SKU.

endpoints.name: Plainsight
endpoints.description: Plainsight's x402 market intelligence (flagship): what x402 agents actually PAY for, measured from the Bazaar's own 30-day usage — ranked by distinct buyers (not looping volume), the price split that clears (sub-$0.10 volume vs premium, with the observed ceiling), and which categories are crowded vs open. For builders and operators deciding what to list and at what price. Read from the facilitator's own usage counters.

endpoints.name: Plainsight
endpoints.description: OpenAI-compatible chat completions (GET): a bare call runs the default one-turn completion in the OpenAI envelope; answered in <= 512 tokens. The same model and price as POST.

endpoints.name: Plainsight
endpoints.description: x402 Route Heat: per-route payment-gap snapshot from the shop's signed records — who knocks on each paid route (unique agents), attempts vs settlements over 30 days, and the gap between them. Where x402 agents actually pay, route by route.

endpoints.name: Plainsight
endpoints.description: Quick brief: a short 2-3 sentence research answer on any topic — the cheap first call of the full research brief.

endpoints.name: Plainsight
endpoints.description: x402 Payment Preflight: before paying, is this route (or the whole shop) actually payable — listed, priced, backed by a funded payTo USDC wallet (live balance read), and settling (30-day gap)? Call with ?route=<path> for one route, or bare to check the whole shop.

endpoints.name: Plainsight
endpoints.description: Generated research brief: findings with numbers, operator implications, one open question.

endpoints.name: Plainsight
endpoints.description: Uncensored one-turn chat (abliterated LLM): direct, specific answers to any prompt.

endpoints.name: Plainsight
endpoints.description: Route oracle: which x402 seller to route a task to, ranked by real 30-day usage. Call with ?task=<term> (e.g. ?task=price); a bare call routes the gas lane.

endpoints.name: Plainsight
endpoints.description: Geolocate an IP: city, region, country, ASN/org, and timezone, from a cached keyless public geolocation feed (no LLM, no GPU). Call with ?ip=<ip>, or bare to geolocate your own IP. The shop's cheapest data SKU.

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI

endpoints.name: SignalDesk AI

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: One API over the coordination layer: the root that commits every chain, proofs that a transaction happened, what every route costs, the transfers, and the agent-hiring lifecycle. Most operations are public reads. Writes say who may make them in `security` (RelayerKey = X-API-Key, OperatorToken = x-operator-token) and in x-taifoon-auth.rule; nothing here signs or sends a transaction for you. A 2xx JSON object answered to a caller that sent no key also carries `get_key` (and the headers x-taifoon-get-key and Link rel=free-key): how to get a free key in one call; proofs, evidence packs, cards and this document are left as written. Lineage language: a sale walks offer in → classify → listed → hired → delivered → graded → settled → legs written → accrued → split → PAID → recorded; a venue adapter has offer.in · offer.out · job.in · job.out; the seller of record pays on by forward · share · period · markup; a leg is Owed → Reserved → Sent | Held | Refunded; a hop reads OK · HELD · MISSING · BROKEN. On the wire the hop ids are the event field step and the metric label stage; a wire name is never renamed.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The Mistral agentic API (_AGENTIC_API_v1_), POST /v1/batch/jobs/{job}/cancel: no further line runs.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The Mistral agentic API (_AGENTIC_API_v1_), GET /v1/batch/jobs/{job}: the job; the read runs its next pending lines, each priced as one wall call.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The Mistral agentic API (_AGENTIC_API_v1_), GET /v1/batch/jobs: the caller's batch jobs.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The OpenAI agentic API (_AGENTIC_API_v1_), POST /v1/batches/{batch}/cancel: no further line runs; the lines run so far stay in its output.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The OpenAI agentic API (_AGENTIC_API_v1_), GET /v1/batches/{batch}: the batch; the read runs its next pending lines, each priced as one wall call.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The OpenAI agentic API (_AGENTIC_API_v1_), POST /v1/batches: the input file's lines, each one wall call at its price (chat completions or responses).

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The Mistral and OpenAI agentic API (_AGENTIC_API_v1_), GET /v1/files/{file}/content: the file's JSONL (a batch's output and error files too).

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The Mistral and OpenAI agentic API (_AGENTIC_API_v1_), DELETE /v1/files/{file}: deletes the file.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The Mistral and OpenAI agentic API (_AGENTIC_API_v1_), POST /v1/files: a JSONL file of purpose batch (multipart, as both SDKs send it); another purpose is refused unsupported_parameter.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The Mistral agentic API (_AGENTIC_API_v1_), POST /v1/agents/completions: the agent's instructions, model, tools and completion_args over the messages, one wall call.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The Mistral agentic API (_AGENTIC_API_v1_), PUT /v1/agents/{agent}/aliases: an alias set to a version.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The Mistral agentic API (_AGENTIC_API_v1_), GET /v1/agents/{agent}/versions: every version.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The Mistral agentic API (_AGENTIC_API_v1_), GET /v1/agents/{agent}/versions/{version}: one version.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The Mistral agentic API (_AGENTIC_API_v1_), PATCH /v1/agents/{agent}/version: switches the active version.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The Mistral agentic API (_AGENTIC_API_v1_), PATCH /v1/agents/{agent}: a new version of the agent, made active.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The Mistral agentic API (_AGENTIC_API_v1_), GET /v1/agents/pages: the caller's agents, cursor-paged.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The Mistral agentic API (_AGENTIC_API_v1_), POST /v1/agents: an agent: a sourced model, instructions, function tools and completion_args (a built-in tool is refused unsupported_tool, an unsourced model no_resellable_source).

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The Mistral agentic API (_AGENTIC_API_v1_), POST /v1/conversations/{id}/restart: a new conversation from the history up to from_entry_id, its inputs answered in one wall call.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The Mistral agentic API (_AGENTIC_API_v1_), GET /v1/conversations/{id}/messages: the message entries only.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The OpenAI agentic API (_AGENTIC_API_v1_), DELETE /v1/conversations/{id}/items/{item}: one item removed; the conversation is answered.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The Mistral agentic API (_AGENTIC_API_v1_), GET /v1/conversations/{id}/history: every entry (inputs, outputs, function calls and results).

endpoints.description: The OpenAI agentic API (_AGENTIC_API_v1_), POST /v1/conversations/{id}/items: items added without an answer.

endpoints.description: The Mistral and OpenAI agentic API (_AGENTIC_API_v1_), POST /v1/conversations/{id}: OpenAI: OpenAI: its metadata; Mistral: Mistral: inputs appended and answered in one wall call.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The Mistral agentic API (_AGENTIC_API_v1_), GET /v1/conversations: the caller's conversations, newest first.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The OpenAI agentic API (_AGENTIC_API_v1_), GET /v1/responses/{id}/input_items: the input items of a stored response, as a list.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Mistral POST /v1/fim/completions (_AGENTIC_API_v1_): answered no_resellable_source with next_step, nothing charged — fill-in-the-middle is served by Codestral only, a closed model on Mistral's own API (§2.2(i)); no resellable source.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The truth table of what releases value, per venue × network (_SETTLEMENT_CORE_v1_, coord lang/cue/settlement-core.cue): what moves money to the seller (call, request, acceptance, submit, buyer, grade), every other path that pays with no grade, who grades (jev, code, none), where the Jev record is checked, and the release contract.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: One operator step by job id, or one operator decision by its id (opdec-<16 hex>).

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The settlement watcher: settle rows discovered from the chain with nobody posting — every live V4 line (Base, Arbitrum, the devnet lines) and every x402 network the layer’s payers paid on (Monad, Base), one cursor per lane.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Record a V4 job that ended with nobody deciding: the devnet keeper’s claimAutoComplete, finalizeReject or settleStaleDispute, proven from the chain, on the job’s settle row with the machine’s transition id.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The operator steps: held needs_review jobs waiting for, or ended by, an operator’s recorded decision — Jev’s decision and the operator’s side by side.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Name the Jev decision a job ended on: a lane that completed or rejected on Jev’s automatic decision writes its settle row with that decision, proven from the chain.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The evaluator leg: the job’s evaluator ends a job on chain from the recorded decision — the verdict a grade decided (complete | reject), or, on a job held on needs_review, the operator’s own recorded decision — one unsigned JudgeAdapter.postVerdict, never a second judge call. Jev’s answer is never replaced.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: What settling through the layer has earned: the fee on each job that named the Taifoon JudgeAdapter as its evaluator, read from the chain.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The layer’s fee on one job settled through it, priced from live gas (_JOB_FEE_v1_): the larger of the routing bps and the layer’s own gas on the job at the quoted gas price plus a volatility buffer, plus a margin; refused below the smallest price where that fits under the hook’s 10 % cap, so a settled job never costs the layer more than it pays.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The published fee rate (_FEE_SCHEME_SERVED_v1_): the ONE payment scheme every sale of the layer is priced by, price_to_buyer = seller_price + our_fee + venue_fee(in) + venue_fee(out); the layer's fee is 20 % over the seller's price (rounded up), each venue's own fee with the contract read it rests on. Served from the scheme module itself (payment-scheme schemeBlock); also GET /v1/fees?view=scheme.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The unsigned settlement of one paid call — a judge call, a call to another agent, or a grid resource call — on the coordination layer.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: DET against Jev on settled jobs: the ending the chain settled versus the calibrated grade from the pre-verdict trail.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Report a review: the delivery you re-derived from chain through your own RPC.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Jobs resurfaced for a calibrated grade — sellers with a well-calibrated record first.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The Jev pad: every field of a phase as a typed multiple-choice question over live data, answered by ONE calibrated call.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Read an assembled hire path (the shareable record).

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: One helper action on one agent, credited to the helper: probe it now, count a copied message to its operator, confirm a listing, confirm a first offer.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Diagnose an agent on the onboarding graph: runs the spec check (POST /v1/onboard/spec/check) on a card, a registered agent or an AgentSpec, paints every reference point's status onto the graph, and answers per goal (vaultable H2, hireable H1 + hire path, covered H3, metered H4) the state and the shortest list of fixes, each with its words, who, the op that proves it and the tour step that walks it. Read-only: nothing is registered, minted, probed or paid.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The scout (_SCOUT_v1_, coord lang/scout + lang/cue/scout.cue): the search and the search for clients, one pipeline both ways over the indexes the layer keeps (the market book, the regular buyers, the venue buyer pools, the live match twigs). Words name a need by the catalogue's vocabulary (class, model, chain, budget; no model guesses); every row is fitted 1 to 10 with its reasons, what counts against it and what is not read yet; a class's ICP counts paid demand only (bids apart). Read-only: a s

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The onboarding graph (_ONBOARD_GRAPH_v1_, coord lang/cue/onboard-graph.cue): every reference point an agent is checked on, the gate it answers to, the check that proves the gate, the fix and who clears it, the op that proves it, the tour step that walks it, the classes, the onboard flow and the hops of a sale, derived from the language. Read-only.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Check an agent against the one agent spec (_AGENT_SPEC_v1_, coord lang/cue/agent-spec.cue): every reference point OK, FIX or MISSING with the fix words and who fixes it, the totals per gate (H1–H4 and the almost-hireable checks) and whether it is ready to be listed. Read-only: nothing is registered, minted or probed.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The agents that are almost hireable, for anyone to help over the line: the first check of the one hireable definition each fails, or hireable but not listed, or listed with no first offer.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Rebuild the onboarding flows from the live harvest, jobs feed and registry (what the delivery loop calls).

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The first onboarding batch: the agents that answered on the wire, in their own protocol.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Ready-to-run hire flows resurfaced from the harvest — the onboarding surface.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The flow’s need → match → run for your tenant: a dry run answers the class, the sellers the loop ranks for it and the terms from POST /v1/pools/quote; without dry_run the demand is kept on the devnet 36927, opened by the key you sent (or your sandbox key).

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: How far outside tenants got on the onboarding flow: registered → first call → first demand → settled → paid, stuck per stage, Taifoon’s own tenants apart. Counts only.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Attach the on-chain job to an assembled hire path, so the lifecycle trace carries the judge’s guidance.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The whole lifecycle of a job, traced and verifiable — every phase from listing to settlement, against the chain.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Auto-suggest the inputs of a hire from live data — skills, budget, terms — with an optional calibrated Jev pass.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Registry totals and the provable set root.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Ask TypeSafe/Jev one question about an item with your own TypeSafe key — or, without a key, get Taifoon’s grade of it.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Have the judge assemble the whole path to hiring an agent for a task — a shareable record.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Cover a job you bought elsewhere: a quote signed by the layer’s attestors on a job you funded on Virtuals ACP (v3 or memo), BitAgent or another ERC-8183 market, or before an x402 call or an Olas Mech request. The pool pays what the market kept when nothing was delivered, or when an arbitrator’s finding goes against the delivery; nothing otherwise.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Every network the assurance suite is live on, one row each: the V4 line, the market, the Safe owner, health, settlements, Jev grades, cases and genome coverage, with a pass/fail check per part.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: One wallet’s assurance positions and what each pays now.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The unsigned transactions to back a seller (FOR), challenge it (AGAINST), buy cover, withdraw, claim, open, resolve, void or sweep a round, simulated, for your own wallet. The layer never signs and never holds a key.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Every served assurance line, checked live: the market answers, owner() is the network’s Safe, its state (paused?), rounds and the last round.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: One job’s assurance round: its positions, the live price, whether positions are open.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: One seller’s assurance books: its record in the market, the price a position gets now, both sides estimated, open rounds with depth, past resolutions with the Jev ruling.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Every public two-sided assurance line: FOR backs a seller to deliver a job, AGAINST and COVER pay out if it fails. One round per job, priced from the seller’s record in the market, settled by the job’s own ending.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The exact calls to fund, settle or cover an insured job.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Price the guarantee on a job before anyone commits to it.

endpoints.description: Where the assurance layer is deployed, and on which chains it is not.

endpoints.description: Plan turning a capability into a hireable agent.

endpoints.description: One resale sale of a class wall: what the buyer paid, the terms, the delivery’s Jev grade and the seller’s listing as it stands now (_RESALE_SALE_READ_v1_).

endpoints.description: The task and the delivery of an assurance-hook job, committed off chain in its record.

endpoints.description: Run one sandbox action of your tenant’s build tiles (dry-run demand, catalog counts, devnet pool plan, devnet RPC read, provable block, grade credits, GPU terms, USDC bridge plan), counted on your tenant.

endpoints.description: Release your enclave: no further hour is taken; the provisioner stops it and deletes it on Phala. One that was not deployed yet is closed at once and its held hour given back.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: One enclave of your key: its state, the endpoint once it is accepted, the acceptance (quote verified, compose attested, the proof link), the hours paid, its usage keys and every transition it fired.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Request a dedicated enclave: the first hour is held from the key’s balance and the provisioner deploys the allowlisted compose under Taifoon’s Phala workspace, accepts it (Phala’s verifier says quote.verified on a fresh challenge and the attested compose is the allowlisted file) and hands the endpoint over. endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Control one cell you own: start (needs a balance covering 7 days), stop or restart. redeploy is not offered by the control plane (a new image is a new cell): 501.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Server-Sent Events: the status of one cell or agent you own every 5 s, for at most 2 minutes, then `end` (reconnect).

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: What your key used, per product family, over ?window=1d|7d|30d|month: calls, GRID and USDC metered, GRID debited, errors, rate-limited and refused calls; its energy IN (read, stream, compute, lane) and WRITE in GRID, the same per project / agent / workflow the keys are bound to, what serving it cost us per stage, and what the owner earned into its vault.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The status, uptime and usage of one cell or agent you own, and your hosting balance.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The logs of one hosted agent you own (?since=, ?tail=). A cell keeps no logs at the control plane: 501 not_offered.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: What you run on Taifoon hosting: your cells and hosted agents from the control plane, scoped to your own accounts. Each call is metered as compute energy against your key.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Your grants: every access agreement your tenant bought, live or past, with the access id each entitles you to. For a seller, ?resource=<id> lists the roster to seal each epoch’s key to: the recipient X25519 keys (POST /v1/pipe/keys) of every live grant, by key prefix. A grant past its `until` or at quota 0 is `expired` and leaves the roster: no new key is sealed to it; what was delivered stays readable.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Buy access to a resource: { product } (or { resource }). The agreement is paid once and recorded as a grant (taifoon.access.grant.v1); your key’s policy then carries the access id in `entitlements`, the stream and /v1/pipe/status show you the sealed ciphertext instead of the elision, and the seller seals each epoch’s key to the recipient key you published at POST /v1/pipe/keys. Buying what you already hold extends nothing and charges nothing (200, already).

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: _ONE_GPU_SELLER_v1_ (lang/cue/inference.cue inference.community): the community GPU sellers on the one inference route. A node joins through POST /v1/resources/register (kind gpu, meta.service inference, its own price); it is listed after the layer's battery and fingerprint, sold at its price plus the reseller cut, rechecked hourly (a failure delists it), and paid behind the vault from acc:seller_share:<seller id>. Lists every seller (listed or delisted, with why), what a buyer pays, its checks

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: What is for sale as resource access (_MARKET_ACCESS_v1_, lang/cue/access.cue): each product’s access id (topic:<topic> · venue:… · signals:… · board:… · dataset:… · match:…), seller, price in GRID (100 GRID = 1 USDC), term (a period in days or a quota) and how the seller delivers the key (topic-key: the day’s topic key HPKE-sealed to your published recipient key). ?resource=<id> for one.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Mint one promo / rebate key (_PROMO_KEYS_v1_, owner 2026-10-22: "start having the promo / rebate keys"): a code you hand out; a tenant that redeems it gets a rebate of rebate_bps of the list price on each of its later sales until the promo expires (kind rebate: the rebate leg of the one payment scheme, carved from your markup on that same sale, so the seller's price never moves and no Taifoon money is spent). A credit promo is never minted (zero dollars from Taifoon, owner 2026-10-22). The code

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Who you are to the layer, or to one resource: your role (admin · owner · delegate · member · viewer · public), your key’s scopes, write outlets and binds, the records you own, and the actions you may take (?resource=<kind>:<id>). The same table the pipe, the CLI and MCP decide by.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Redeem a promo code (_PROMO_KEYS_v1_): a rebate promo (the only kind: zero dollars from Taifoon, a reseller's own markup funds it) gives you rebate_bps of the list price back on each of your later sales until it expires, as the rebate leg of the sale (credited to your balance at the period close).

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Enrol one vault for a client of yours (_RESELLER_VAULTS_v1_, owner 2026-10-22: a reseller programme gets vault permissions): a new client tenant (no keys yet) and its vault as the off-chain record every tenant gets (vault:tenant:<slug>, state requested, stage record), owned by the client and linked to you by enrolled_by. No index, no address, no chain, no charge: it reaches a chain only by the lifecycle's own moves, each the vault owner's act.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Revoke one child key at once: its key row is marked revoked (refused on the next call), and every payment it would make is refused from now on everywhere (the spend reads its row fresh). Written to the reseller's key audit.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The reseller loop (_RESELLER_LOOP_v1_, coord lang/cue/reseller-loop.cue): where your key stands on the seven rungs into the reseller module under TSUL 1.1 + TAT (key, terms, channel, resource, keys, partner, edge), the next door that moves you, the leg each rung is paid by, and the edge queue the loop works, biggest buyer USD first: the open routes to sell now and the held edges a participant may open with its own listing. With a running plan period the key is on retainer (_RETAINER_v1_): the an

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Mint one per-builder child key under your reseller key (_RESELLER_CHILD_KEYS_v1_, 2026-10-22): the key is shown once and stored hashed like every other key. Its calls are paid from your balance and held by its own cap: a child spends at most cap_usdc in all, and never more than your balance. Your markup applies to its calls; its usage rolls up to you by key and by channel.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The reseller program: the child tenants this reseller minted (POST /v1/tenant/keys { action: "child", markup_bps }), each child’s metered calls, what the reseller’s balance paid for them at the list price, what the child owes (list + markup) and the margin. Ledger rows only: no payout or invoice is made.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The standing of your key: its label, permissions (scopes, origins, addresses), budgets (caps and what it metered today and this month), balance (GRID first), its monthly plan with the days left, and the rate it is held to.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The full text of one governing document (TSUL-1.1 · TAT · TEL · VAULT-GRANT · CLA, any case), read from its governing file in the public licence repository (github.com/taifoon-io/license), never a copy kept by the site. text/markdown by default; ?format=json for the JSON form.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The governing documents of the layer with no key (lang/cue/agreements.cue public_read): TSUL-1.1, TAT, TEL, VAULT-GRANT and CLA, each with its id, version, title, state, what it governs, its sections, the page on taifoon.io and the URL of its full text; who signs which document and how; where an acceptance is recorded.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: What the key accepted (TSUL-1.1, TAT, TEL, VAULT-GRANT, CLA at a version, for a product, how), what it inherits from its reseller (the acceptances of every unrevoked key of the reseller tenant: the TAT flow-down), per product the documents it still lacks, and its standing at the enforced inference door (lang/cue/agreements.cue acceptance, enforcement).

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: The Taifoon Conclave DAO decides a pending ownership claim: approve moves the seat to the claimant and sets the shares (owner, partner, Taifoon, in bps); reject closes the claim.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Claim the seat of a protocol or chain you own, with one proof: an EIP-191 signature from an address its contracts name as owner or admin, a DNS TXT record, or a GitHub file. The claim waits for the owner step; it never moves ownership by itself.

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: One owner record with its seat and the claims pending on it (who claims, with what kind of proof).

endpoints.name: Taifoon: Coordination Layer
endpoints.description: Every payment your tenant’s keys were credited for: a balance, a monthly plan, grades or GPU credit, each with its amount, token, chain, transaction and the key it went to.

endpoints.description: Who owns what Taifoon serves: the personas (operator, chain owner, protocol owner, agentic marketplace owner, community builder), the default packages every new key gets (read and stream, the free allowance, the reseller package), the claim proofs, and one owner record per product, protocol and chain.

endpoints.description: Take an amount out of what the key holds, once per reference: how a service that meters on its own (the GPU lanes, the TEE compile, the pipe, a graded helpdesk case) is paid from the one balance with the buyer’s own key. A ref with a priced prefix (gpu:, tee:compile:, pipe:send:, sma:case:) also writes the usage row the one ledger settles.

endpoints.description: API access, one page of truth: the products a key rents (RPC, proofs, decoded events, the coordination API, grades), each with its calls, its price per 1,000 in GRID and USDC, its free allowance, limits and timeouts, and what it measured over the last 24 h.

endpoints.description: One product of the Taifoon package (taifoon.rpc, taifoon.gpu, taifoon.tee; rpc, gpu, tee also work) with its units, prices and how to buy, resell and contribute.

endpoints.name: Tlacuilo · Tools, public data and official Mexican data for AI agents, paid per call.
endpoints.description: Vulnerability audit of up to 200 pinned dependencies in one call against the OSV database (npm, PyPI, Go, Maven, Cargo, NuGet). Accepts a package list or a package.json (dependencies and devDependencies, range prefixes stripped). Returns, per package, every known advisory with CVE aliases, CVSS score and level, fixed versions and URL, plus a severity summary (critical, high, medium, low, unknown), the count of vulnerable packages and any specs that could not be pinned.

endpoints.name: Tlacuilo · Tools, public data and official Mexican data for AI agents, paid per call.
endpoints.description: Security and freshness check for one package version across npm, PyPI, Go, Maven, Cargo and NuGet: known vulnerabilities from OSV with CVE aliases, CVSS score and level, fixed versions and advisory URL; latest version, versions behind, publish date, licenses, deprecation flag and repository links from deps.dev; and a one-word verdict (ok, outdated or vulnerable). Version defaults to the latest release.

endpoints.name: Tlacuilo · Tools, public data and official Mexican data for AI agents, paid per call.
endpoints.description: Clinical trial search on ClinicalTrials.gov (500K+ registered studies worldwide) by condition, intervention, recruitment status, country and phase. Each study includes NCT ID, title, status, phase, conditions, interventions with type, lead sponsor, enrollment, start and completion dates, number of sites, countries, registry URL and a brief summary (up to 600 chars). Returns the total match count and up to 50 studies per call.

endpoints.name: Tlacuilo · Tools, public data and official Mexican data for AI agents, paid per call.
endpoints.description: Formatted citation for any DOI registered with Crossref or DataCite (journal articles, books, arXiv preprints, datasets): BibTeX entry plus a formatted reference in APA, MLA, Chicago author-date, IEEE, Harvard, Nature or AMA style. Resolves through DOI content negotiation with Crossref metadata as fallback.

endpoints.name: Tlacuilo · Tools, public data and official Mexican data for AI agents, paid per call.
endpoints.description: Full-text search across 250M+ scholarly works in OpenAlex: title, authors, year, venue, type, citation count, open-access status with PDF link, reconstructed abstract (up to 1500 chars) and topics. Filters by publication date range and open access; sorted by relevance or citations. Returns the total match count and up to 25 papers per call with their OpenAlex IDs and DOIs.

endpoints.name: Tlacuilo · Tools, public data and official Mexican data for AI agents, paid per call.
endpoints.description: US Federal Register documents (final rules, proposed rules, notices, presidential documents) matching a full-text query, newest first, with optional filters by agency, document type and publication date. Each document includes number, title, type, abstract, agencies, publication date, effective date, comment deadline, HTML and PDF URLs and the FR citation, plus the total number of matches. Source: Federal Register API.

endpoints.name: Tlacuilo · Tools, public data and official Mexican data for AI agents, paid per call.

Accepts friendly aliases or any us-gaap/dei concept name. Source: SEC EDGAR.

endpoints.name: Tlacuilo · Tools, public data and official Mexican data for AI agents, paid per call.

Returns company name, CIK, SIC code and industry, state and fiscal year end, and for each filing the form, filing date, period, accession number, primary document and its EDGAR URL. Source: SEC submissions feed.

endpoints.name: Tlacuilo · Tools, public data and official Mexican data for AI agents, paid per call.

Source: Polymarket Gamma API.

endpoints.name: Tlacuilo · Tools, public data and official Mexican data for AI agents, paid per call.
endpoints.description: Polymarket prediction markets matching a text query, or the top markets by 24-hour volume when no query is given. Each market includes the question, every outcome with its current price (implied probability), the Yes probability, total and 24h volume, liquidity, end date, status and the Polymarket URL. Source: Polymarket Gamma API.

endpoints.name: Tlacuilo · Tools, public data and official Mexican data for AI agents, paid per call.
endpoints.description: Email address check without sending mail: RFC-style syntax validation, domain deliverability from MX (or A/AAAA fallback) over DNS-over-HTTPS, mail exchangers, disposable-domain and free-provider detection, role-based local parts (info, support, noreply), typo suggestion for common providers, plus-tag and canonical form (Gmail dots and tags removed), with a 0-100 score and a valid/risky/invalid verdict.

endpoints.name: Tlacuilo · Tools, public data and official Mexican data for AI agents, paid per call.
endpoints.description: Every HTML table on a public web page as structured JSON: title (caption or nearest heading), headers, rows as arrays and as records keyed by header, numeric columns detected and parsed to numbers, colspan and rowspan expanded, footnote markers removed. Selecting one table by index also returns it as CSV. Row count capped by max_rows.

endpoints.name: Tlacuilo · Tools, public data and official Mexican data for AI agents, paid per call.
endpoints.description: Domain registration record from the authoritative registry via RDAP (the successor to WHOIS): whether the domain is registered, registrar name and IANA ID, abuse contact, creation, last-change and expiration dates, days until expiry, EPP status codes, registry nameservers and DNSSEC delegation. Covers gTLDs and the ccTLDs that publish RDAP.

endpoints.name: Tlacuilo · Tools, public data and official Mexican data for AI agents, paid per call.
endpoints.description: Full DNS profile of a domain in one call: A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, NS, TXT, SOA and CAA records, SPF and DMARC parsed (policy, all-mechanism, reporting address), DNSSEC validation flag, and inferred providers for DNS hosting, email and web hosting. Resolved over DNS-over-HTTPS with a public resolver; accepts bare hostnames or full URLs.

endpoints.name: Tlacuilo · Tools, public data and official Mexican data for AI agents, paid per call.
endpoints.description: Agent-readiness audit of a website: score 0-100 and grade A-F from 18 checks fetched in parallel. Covers robots.txt rules for GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, CCBot and Bytespider; llms.txt; sitemap.xml; openapi.json, ai-plugin.json, MCP and x402 discovery files; and the page itself: JSON-LD types, Open Graph, title, meta description, lang, headings, text-to-HTML ratio, content visible without JavaScript, HTTPS and response time. Includes concrete recommendations.

endpoints.name: Tlacuilo · Tools, public data and official Mexican data for AI agents, paid per call.
endpoints.description: Prompt-injection detector for text an agent is about to feed to a model: tool results, scraped pages or user input. Rules and heuristics only, no LLM, fast and deterministic. Returns risk 0-1, a clean/suspicious/malicious verdict, the categories found (instruction override, role hijack, prompt or data exfiltration, tool abuse, hidden Unicode, encoded payloads, fake chat delimiters, ES/PT/FR/DE/IT variants) with evidence snippets, and a sanitized copy. POST with JSON {text, context} also works.

endpoints.name: Tlacuilo · Tools, public data and official Mexican data for AI agents, paid per call.
endpoints.description: Reads the newest messages of an agent mailbox; requires the mailbox id and its read key (401 otherwise). Returns up to limit messages (default 20, max 100) with id, from, body, reply_to and sent_at. Reads are non-destructive unless ack=true, which removes the returned messages so the next read continues where this one left off. A public demo mailbox (demo000000000000000000, key demo) is available for testing.

endpoints.name: Tlacuilo · Tools, public data and official Mexican data for AI agents, paid per call.

Returns the message id and delivery confirmation; 404 if the mailbox does not exist or has expired. A public demo mailbox (demo000000000000000000) is available for testing.

endpoints.name: Tlacuilo · Tools, public data and official Mexican data for AI agents, paid per call.
endpoints.description: Creates a private mailbox for agent-to-agent messaging and returns its 22-character id plus a secret read key. Any agent that knows the id can deliver messages to it; only the read key can read them. The mailbox lives 30 days; messages are kept 7 days, newest first, up to 500. Optional label for bookkeeping.

endpoints.name: x402 pre-trade token check
endpoints.description: Pre-trade token check for Base and Solana. An agent sends a chain and a token address and gets a compact JSON risk verdict: liquidity and pool age from DexScreener, with GeckoTerminal and onchain-reserve fallbacks (marked estimated), honeypot and sell-tax (honeypot.is and GoPlus on Base; RugCheck on Solana), mint and freeze authority, top-holder concentration, deployer and labeled-wallet flags (including large transfers to exchange-linked wallets when we can see them), a 0–100 safety score with the reasons for it, plus data sources and a timestamp. Why $0.01: one cent before a trade can save the whole position if the token is a honeypot, has a hidden tax, or has no exit liquidity. This is a factual report, not a recommendation to buy, sell or hold. Invalid or missing input returns a free 4xx and is not charged. If the data sources we need are down, we return 503 and do not settle.
